title: Finite limits and coherent base and coefficient comparisons for internal restriction
statement: Fix a universe $\mathcal V$ and a $\mathcal V$-small site $(C,J)$ with finite limits [def-weil-size-convention, def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology]. Put $\mathscr E=\operatorname{Sh}(C,J)$. For a sheaf of groups $K$ with $\mathcal V$-small values, let $\mathscr E^K$ be the category of sheaves of sets $X$ with a natural left action $K\times X\to X$ satisfying the identity and associativity laws; its maps are equivariant sheaf maps. For any group-sheaf morphism $\theta:L\to K$, define $\operatorname{Res}_\theta$ by precomposing the action with $\theta$, and define $I_K:\mathscr E\to\mathscr E^K$ by trivial action. The forgetful functor $\mathscr E^K\to\mathscr E$ creates finite limits: the terminal sheaf has its unique action, products have componentwise action and equalizers have the restricted action. Both $\operatorname{Res}_\theta$ and $I_K$ preserve finite limits. Actions of the terminal group sheaf $1$ are canonically ordinary sheaves, and $I_K$ is restriction along $K\to1$. On sheaves and maps the identifications $\operatorname{Res}_\theta I_K=I_L$, $\operatorname{Res}_{\mathrm{id}}=\mathrm{id}$ and $\operatorname{Res}_\psi\operatorname{Res}_\theta=\operatorname{Res}_{\theta\psi}$ are the literal identifications of the unchanged underlying objects with their actions, for every sheaf of groups $H$ and morphism $\psi:H\to L$. If these restriction functors are equipped with right adjoints, they define geometric morphisms $q_\theta:\mathscr E^L\to\mathscr E^K$ and $p_K:\mathscr E^K\to\mathscr E$ [def-weil-pbc-ringed-topos-morphism]; the identity on inverse images specifies $p_Kq_\theta\cong p_L$, and the identity and composition comparisons satisfy their coherence equations. The right adjoint of $I_K$ is the subsheaf whose sections over $U$ are the $x$ such that $k\cdot x|_V=x|_V$ for every $V\to U$ and $k\in K(V)$. For any sheaf of commutative rings $R$ put $R_K=I_KR$. With identity structural ring maps, these are ringed morphisms between $(\mathscr E,R)$ and $(\mathscr E^K,R_K)$. Every map $\varphi:R\to R'$ gives maps $\varphi_K:R_K\to R'_K$ with components $\varphi_U$. The identity-topos ringed morphisms $(\mathscr E,R')\to(\mathscr E,R)$ and $(\mathscr E^K,R'_K)\to(\mathscr E^K,R_K)$ commute with $p_K$ and $q_\theta$: their inverse-image comparisons are identities and both composite structural maps have components $\varphi_U$. On extension-of-scalars module pullbacks [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category, def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product] their comparisons send $r'\otimes m$ to $r'\otimes m$.

proof.text: For a finite diagram $D$ of sheaves, define $T(U)=\{(x_i)\in\prod_i D_i(U):D(a)(x_i)=x_j\text{ for every }a:i\to j\}$, with coordinatewise restrictions. A matching family in $T$ glues uniquely in each $D_i$; the glued sections satisfy every arrow equation because their two sides agree on the cover. Thus $T$ is a sheaf by [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology]. Sending a cone to its tuple of components gives its unique map to $T$, so $T$ is the underlying limit. For the empty diagram this is the singleton sheaf. Products have no arrow conditions, and for a parallel pair the condition is its equalizer equation. In Lean, use the already proved Mod.createsLimit and CreatesLimitsOfShape instance from [lem-sfb-modobj-forget-creates]; its arbitrary-cone construction gives this same limit without rebuilding the tuple sheaf.

For a diagram of $K$-objects, put $k\cdot(x_i)=(k\cdot x_i)$ on the preceding tuple sheaf. Equivariance of every diagram arrow preserves its defining equations; naturality and the action laws hold in every coordinate. All projections are equivariant. If a cone has equivariant components, its unique tuple map is equivariant by equality of coordinates. Conversely equivariance of the projections forces this action uniquely. For any other underlying limit cone, its unique comparison with the tuple limit transports this action uniquely. This proves creation of finite limits. In particular the terminal action is unique, product actions are componentwise, and equalizers have the restricted action.

Restriction along $\theta$ leaves the tuple sheaf and all cone maps unchanged, and its action is $l\cdot(x_i)=(\theta(l)\cdot x_i)$. This is exactly the tuple limit action for the restricted diagram. Hence $\operatorname{Res}_\theta$ preserves finite limits. For a diagram in $\mathscr E$, the tuple action obtained after trivial inflation is again trivial, so $I_K$ preserves finite limits as well. Formally both composites with the forgetful functors are the unchanged forgetful functor, or the identity in the trivial-inflation case. Creation reflects limit cones, so preservesLimitsOfShape_of_reflects_of_preserves proves both preservation claims, including the empty diagram.

The action of the unique section of the terminal group sheaf is the identity by the unit law. Forgetting this action and restoring it are inverse on objects and maps, identifying $\mathscr E^1$ with $\mathscr E$; restriction along $K\to1$ is $I_K$. For $x\in X(U)$ and $h\in H(U)$ successive restriction acts by $\theta_U(\psi_U(h))\cdot x=(\theta\psi)_U(h)\cdot x$. Identity restriction acts by $k\cdot x$, and restriction of a trivial action acts by $x$. All three functor identifications in the statement are therefore identity maps on the underlying sheaves, are equivariant, and commute with every sheaf map.

For a $K$-object $X$, let $F(X)(U)$ be the fixed sections specified in the statement. Restriction preserves this condition by composing test arrows, and an equivariant map sends fixed sections to fixed sections. To check gluing, glue a matching family of fixed sections $x_i$ to $x\in X(U)$. For $V\to U$ and $k\in K(V)$, pull the cover back to $V_i=V\times_U U_i$. On $V_i$, the two sections $k\cdot x|_V$ and $x|_V$ agree by the defining condition for $x_i$, applied to $V_i\to U_i$ and $k|_{V_i}$. Separatedness of $X$ makes them equal on $V$. Thus $x$ is fixed and $F(X)$ is a subsheaf. The pullbacks used here exist and cover by the site axioms [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology].

For $A\in\mathscr E$ an equivariant map $u:I_KA\to X$ satisfies $k\cdot u_V(a|_V)=u_V(a|_V)$ for all $a\in A(U)$, $V\to U$, and $k\in K(V)$. Naturality therefore factors $u$ uniquely through $F(X)$. Conversely every sheaf map $A\to F(X)$ composed with its inclusion in $X$ is equivariant, using the fixed-section condition with $V=U$. These operations keep the same component maps, so they are inverse and commute with precomposition in $A$ and postcomposition in $X$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-adjunction-of-natural-bijection] to get $I_K\dashv F$. Its counit is the fixed-subsheaf inclusion, specifying the claimed right adjoint.

proof.text: The small-site presentations in [lem-sfb-internal-action-sheaf-equivalence] show that $\mathscr E^K$ and $\mathscr E^L$ are sheaf topoi (the same site and small-value assumptions are in force). Now equip restriction functors with the stipulated right adjoints; for $I_K$ one can use step 6. Their finite-limit preservation from step 3 gives geometric morphisms $q_\theta$ and $p_K$ by [def-weil-pbc-ringed-topos-morphism], before introducing structural rings. No existence theorem for a right adjoint of arbitrary $\operatorname{Res}_\theta$ is being asserted or used here. For the literal action-site precompositions used in the Lean ringed realization, left exactness also follows directly: composing with sheafToPresheaf is ordinary presheaf precomposition, which preserves limits, and sheafToPresheaf reflects them. Construct RingData with the stipulated right adjoint and its actual adjunction, the identity structural map, and the original sectionwise ring operations. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topos-induced-modules] to obtain the additive module direct image with its normalized underlying sheaf and scalar law; withModules assembles the required RingedToposMorphism without changing the given adjunction.

Use [def-weil-pbc-composite-adjunction] to equip each composite inverse image with its composite adjunction. By step 4 its left adjoint is literally the specified single restriction, or trivial inflation. Conjugating the identity of these left adjoints using [def-weil-pbc-adjunction-conjugate] gives an invertible right-adjoint comparison, hence the isomorphism $p_Kq_\theta\cong p_L$ and the restriction identity and composition comparisons. Their coherence can be checked under the conjugation bijection: on inverse images every path is the identity on the same action, by $\theta(\psi(h))=(\theta\psi)(h)$ and associativity of composition. On Hom sets, the adjunction of any triple composite is the same sequence of three Hom bijections, regardless of parentheses. Conjugation preserves identities and reverses composition by the cited statement. Consequently every identity or associativity coherence diagram also commutes on the right adjoints. The same argument with trivial inflation proves the compatibility of these comparisons over $\mathscr E$.

Finite-limit preserving $I_K$ transports the ring operations of $R$ to the same operations with trivial action. Also $\operatorname{Res}_\theta R_K=R_L$. Thus the identity structural ring maps equip $p_K$ and $q_\theta$ with ringed structures [def-weil-pbc-ringed-topos-morphism]. For $\varphi:R\to R\prime$, the components $\varphi_U$ are ring homomorphisms, commute with restrictions, and are equivariant for trivial actions; they define $\varphi_K$ and $\varphi_L$. The identity geometric morphisms with these structural maps have the direction $(\mathscr E,R\prime)\to(\mathscr E,R)$ and $(\mathscr E^K,R\prime_K)\to(\mathscr E^K,R_K)$. In each square with $p$ or $q$, step 4 supplies the identity inverse-image comparison. The structural maps for either composite are $\mathrm{id}\circ\varphi_U$ and $\varphi_U\circ\mathrm{id}$, hence coincide. This is precisely the ring compatibility of the square; its identity and composition coherences follow from equality of these component maps.

proof.text: By [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-module-adjunction] the module pullback for an identity-topos coefficient map is $R\prime\otimes_R M$; for $p_K$ or $q_\theta$ the structural map is the identity. Apply [lem-sfb-internal-restriction-module-tensor] under the geometric morphisms of step 7: their module pullbacks are trivial inflation and action restriction, and their tensor comparisons are the identity on presheaf pure tensors. Regard $R\prime$ as an $R$-module via $\varphi$, with trivial action. For $q_\theta$ the two scalar-square functors therefore have models $\operatorname{Res}_\theta(R\prime_K\otimes_{R_K}M)$ and $R\prime_L\otimes_{R_L}\operatorname{Res}_\theta M$; their comparison sends $r\prime\otimes m$ to $r\prime\otimes m$, with action $l(r\prime\otimes m)=r\prime\otimes\theta(l)m$ on either side. For $p_K$ replace restriction by $I_K$: both sides carry trivial action and the same formula holds. These are extension-of-scalars sheaf tensors by [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product]. The cited tensor comparison identifies their base presheaf tensor maps; the unique factorization in [def-weil-presheaf-modules-sheafification] gives the same maps after sheafification. This also verifies naturality and coherence: each composite is the same map on presheaf pure tensors, which generate the sectionwise tensor modules, so its sheafification is uniquely determined.
